title: Godot or Unity for a first commercial 2D game in 2026?
body: A solo developer or a team of two is about to commit to an engine for a first commercial 2D game, and the choice is hard to reverse once art, code and tooling pile up. Which of Godot and Unity are you picking, and what decided it?

Two facts from the vendors themselves frame the choice. The [Godot homepage](https://godotengine.org/) calls it a free, open-source 2D and 3D game engine and makes no other pricing statement. The [Unity homepage](https://unity.com/) says you can get started for free or find a plan, and lists desktop, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, Xbox, Meta Quest, web and Apple Vision Pro as platforms, without showing plan figures.

Console and mobile reach, asset store dependence, scripting language preference and how much you trust a license to stay stable all tend to matter more than raw 2D features. If you shipped or abandoned a 2D project in either engine, share what the deciding factor was and what you would check earlier next time.
